_comment: The journal (issue #114, scripts/journal.gd, key I). Everything the Quests, People, Codex and History tabs show that is not already in another data file lives here, so each chapter adds its entries without code. CONDITIONS ("when", "unlock", "starts", "done", "defeat") use Story.meets keys (active, cleared, not_cleared, seen, joined, renown, held, owns, day) plus journal keys: command (true = the Command Table is running), region (a region id that is open), enemy_seen (an enemy kind met in the field), defeated (an enemy kind beaten at least once), erased_any (true = some province has been erased), plans (true = Verity has aimed the Blank at least once), ink (an Ink colour one of your field heroes uses). CHAPTERS: id, title, starts and done (conditions), recap (paragraphs, each shown once its when holds). The chapter on screen is the last one whose starts holds; story goals in data/story.json name their chapter with "chapter". CODEX: one entry per thing. id (unique, never reuse: read markers are saved by id), cat (places, factions, enemies, blank, inks), title, text (shown once unlocked), more (extra paragraphs with their own when), unlock (conditions; defaults: region entries need their region open, factions need their home province's region open, enemies need enemy_seen of their kind, inks need ink of their colour). Links: region, faction, enemy, ink. Enemy entries also have habits (always shown) and weakness (shown once the defeat condition holds; default defeated of their kind). PROVINCES: extra paragraphs for a province's codex page (province id -> list of {when, text}); the page itself is built from data/provinces.json. FIGURES: people met who never join (villains and townsfolk) for the People tab: id, name, title, portrait (assets/portraits id), text, unlock, more.

recap.text: The Blank eats everything it touches: grass, roads, names, the paperwork that says a thing exists. It does not give things back. It gave you back. You came to in the Frayed Meadow with no name, no voice and no entry in the Great Ledger, and the Nibblers wanted you returned like a library book.

You drove them off. A sellsword called Brannoc Tolley, Bran to anyone he has not yet invoiced, watched you do it, smelled a business opportunity, and walked you to the nearest town to work out what you were worth.

Hollowmark's tax office tried to write you down and found nothing to write. A person who is not in the Ledger is, by statute, a violation, so the Concord wardens locked you up for existing without authorisation.

That night the Blank ate the east wall of the tax office. Bran came in through the hole with a key and an invoice. You fought your way out past the wardens, and by dawn the office was a neat white crater with a few desks still being filed at the rim.

A woman in a pale archivist's coat watched the crater with professional interest, called you 'the one it gave back', and stepped into the white as if it were a door. Governor Thale fled with the town seal and forgot the town. With no governor and no legal standing, Hollowmark could be run by nobody. You are nobody. Quill pointed you at the Command Table.
Tobble brought rumours: a hedge-witch selling cures out of a hollow tree in the Gutterwoods, and a Concord corporal with nine fingers hiding on the Tithe Road after refusing an Erasure order.
Mother Gristle came to Hollowmark with her kettle, her opinions and a cure for most things, including people.
Corporal Daro, Ninefingers, came in off the Tithe Road with a Concord price on their head, the sharpest tongue in the Inklands, and a deserter's knowledge of where Concord forms are weakest.
The Concord answered: a writ nailed to the well announced that a tithe column under Tithe-Captain Morrow would collect all outstanding sums from Hollowmark. The outstanding sum was everyone in it.
You broke the column at Old Mill Crossing. Its strongbox was empty, because it had come to be filled. In Morrow's papers was an order sealed with a red quill: the mark of the Auditor.
The Auditor waited at the Tithe Road tollgate with a quill the length of a lance, striking out anything in his way. He did not strike out Hollowmark. You struck him out instead.

Three days later a letter appeared on the Command Table under a smooth white stone. Verity Hale thanked you for the Auditor, told you she was not your enemy, and asked you, fondly, to stop pushing the white back. It is only trying to help, she says. Hollowmark holds. For now, that is enough.

The night after Verity's letter, every bell in the north began to ring at once, and the fog lifted over Saint Ledger's Abbey. The monks there copy the Great Ledger by hand so that the world can be written back if the capital's copy burns.

Brother Odo walked down from the Abbey in worn-out sandals. The Concord had sent him back with a receipt. The Abbot has his monks copying day and night, and the pages come out blank. Meanwhile the Erasers, Verity's white-coated followers, were burning the wax barges at Candleford, the lake town that lights the Abbey.

You held Candleford's jetty and kept the last of six wax barges afloat. Nell Tapper, chandler and accidental mayor, handed you the town. The Erasers left a list of names pinned to a post, signed by Askew, First Reader.
Prioress Ebba refused to deal with a town run by passers-by. Once Candleford had a governor she invited you to the Abbey, and told you to come armed.

In the copying hall forty monks wrote on blank pages, and Abbot Wulfstan wrote on the air. He called it fidelity. The Prioress asked you to find Sister Osyth, the crypt-keeper of the Bonefield Cloister, who might know why the ink will not hold.

You broke the Erasers' camp on the Bonefield and found Osyth counting skulls: eleven thousand four hundred and six. Verity was waiting behind the Founders' Door with an unedited page. Three hundred years ago the valley refused a tithe, the Concord answered, and the Abbey was built over the dead on a hill the Ledger calls empty. Verity did not fight. She looked at an empty corner as if it had spoken, and walked into the wall.
Told the truth about the Bonefield, the Abbot locked the copying hall and copied himself. The Prioress would not let outsiders near him until the Abbey trusted you.

You found the real Abbot among his copies by the ink on his hands. He is buried by the Founders' Door with the eleven thousand. The Abbey has stopped copying the Ledger and started copying Osyth's board, heading and all. That night Verity thanked you for counting them. Under her name, in someone else's ink, was a single black bar.

A gilt card arrived from the Marquise de Saulx, inviting the person who does not exist to the masquerade on the Velvet Causeway, which has not stopped since the Blank came. Folded inside it was a second note in a rough hand: the quay is going under, come quick.

At Lantern Quay a cabaret singer was holding a bridge of light over a hole the Blank had bitten in the wharf. You kept the eels off Saffron Kiss until forty-one dockfolk and a goat were across. Her songs make things real for as long as she sings, and she has never finished one. She came to Hollowmark to see a town that stays put.

Saffron told you what the scandal sheets do not print: every night a few guests go upstairs to pay their respects to the masquerade's host, and they do not come down. The door only opens for whoever sends the wine, so you went after the Vauclair Terraces.

You went to the masquerade in a plain white mask. Hortense de Saulx, the Velvet Marquise, danced with you in front of the whole Causeway. Verity watched from a balcony, said the hungry thing at the party was not hers, and was gone. When the bell rang for the next course, the revellers turned on the guests, and Hortense turned on the revellers. She came back to Hollowmark with you.

On Pendower Shallows you found Nan Cripps running a shell game on the word-fishers, and her shadow, Tally, telling them where the word really was. Tally is Nan's conscience, signed over to a moneylender when she was fifteen. Both of them work for Hollowmark now. Only one of them is honest about the pay.

Hortense led you onto the smugglers' wharf after midnight, to a Concord barge with a steel table on deck labelled for the unregistered subject. She had been the Concord's spy from the first invitation: deliver you to the Office of Corrections for study, and her sister Bérénice would go free. Then she read the Concord's letter aloud to the whole wharf, tore it up and helped you sink the barge. The letter also said the Concord had been feeding debtors to the masquerade's host to keep the Blank off the bridges.

At the head of the masquerade's table sat the Host, mostly mouth, eating guests to keep the ink lake down. You ended the party. The Causeway has to keep its feet dry the ordinary way now. Verity's letter said the Host was not hers, and that someone else is setting places at the table. Under her name, someone had drawn two black bars.

A fishing boat came up the Hollowmark road on a cart with a piece of the sea in it, cut out with a saw. Harbourmaster Loveday Pascoe of Trevail had brought it to prove what nobody inland believed: five nights ago the whole coast stopped mid-wave, and the boats out past the bar kept sailing, on into the white.

Under the wave that hangs over Trevail, you kept the sea's walking leftovers off the bell tower while Pascoe rang the boats home. Eleven of thirty-two came about. Trevail does not write 'lost' in the harbour book. It writes 'out'.

At Halfwave the tide stands twenty yards off the beach in a green wall, and the drowned walk out of it crusted in salt. In the chapel's looking-glass for the dead you found Dame Ilse: the reflection of a knight the Blank took off the beach, left behind with everything back to front. She stepped out of the glass and came to Hollowmark, looking for a better mirror.

Kerra Hocking walked forty miles from Polgarrow to say her father, the keeper, has not come down from the dark lamp since the sea stopped, and talks all night in a voice with gaps in it. He says your name. The one you have not got.

In Polgarrow's lamp room the keeper spoke in something else's voice: plates, larders, a supper soon, a door left open. Ilse called it a hole talking through a man. Lighting the lamp brought Jory Hocking back with no memory of it. Quill wrote the words down and the ink ran into black bars, all but three: back, supper, door.

Elsewhere, Verity Hale found chalk rings on her map round Polgarrow, Halfwave and Trevail that she did not draw. She began a letter to explain, burned it, and drew the rings again herself so that the map would be correct.

On the sea bed of Halfwave you broke Low Water, everything the tide forgot to bring back, wrecks and all. The tide has started to move again, slow as cold treacle. For the first time no letter from Verity came. Someone drew three black bars in the dust where it would have been.

codex.title: The Brack Marches
codex.text: Farmland, marsh and wood around Hollowmark, on the eastern edge of everything. Pastoral from a distance. Up close the grass grows in half-sentences, the fences end in mid-air, and the horizon is a little closer every week. The Concord never cared much for the Marches. It taxed them, which it considers caring.

codex.title: Saint Ledger's Abbey
codex.text: The north, across the Candle Sound. Bells that ring the hours of a liturgy older than the Concord, and monks who copy the Great Ledger by hand, forever, in ink mixed with their own blood, so that if the capital's copy burns the world can be written back. Lately the pages come out blank, and the monks are running out of both.

codex.title: The Velvet Causeway
codex.text: A bridge-city strung across a lake of ink, where the nobility have been holding the same masquerade since the Blank arrived, on the theory that the end of the world is less likely to interrupt a party it has not been invited to. The music carries for miles. So does the smell of the lake.

codex.title: The Unfinished Coast
codex.text: A shoreline the Blank has half-read. The sea stops mid-wave, ships sail east into the white and nobody writes back, and every province here frays a little faster for it: the sea forgets itself, and the land forgets with it.

codex.title: The Gilded Spire
codex.text: The capital, at the far end of the Tithe Road. Gold on the outside, rot on the inside, and the Great Ledger in the middle: the book in which the Gilded Concord writes down what is true. If the Ledger says a town is fine, the town is fine. If it says a person never existed, they never did.

codex.title: The Mercenary Guild
codex.text: The Guild holds the Gallows Ferry and charges you to cross the river in either direction, which is the most honest business arrangement left in the Marches. They have no politics. They have rates. A Guild contract outlives kings, governors and, so far, the Blank.

codex.title: The Gutterwood Coven
codex.text: Witches who grow trees from discarded letters: every apology never sent, every confession torn up, takes root in the Gutterwoods sooner or later. They decide who leaves the woods, and they dislike visitors, flags, and anything that lets the Blank closer to their trees.

more.text: Mother Gristle was a Coven witch until she started selling cures to people the Coven had decided not to cure. They wanted her gone. You took her in. They have opinions about that.

codex.title: The Gilded Concord
codex.text: The bureaucratic empire that rules from the Gilded Spire and keeps the Great Ledger. Debts are inked onto skin, history is corrected weekly, and Erasure, the striking of a person or a town out of the Ledger, is a legal penalty. To the Concord, an unregistered town run by someone who crawled out of the Blank is not a rebellion. It is a paperwork emergency, which is worse.

more.text: They sent a tithe column to collect Hollowmark. It went home lighter.
They sent the Auditor. He did not go home at all. The Concord does not forget a missing Auditor. It files him, and then it sends someone with a larger quill.

codex.title: Nibbler
codex.text: A small hungry scrap of the Blank: a mouth that has not finished deciding what the rest of it is. Nibblers wander the edges of the white and chase anything that still has a name.
codex.habits: Chases, stops, winds up for half a second, then lunges in a straight line. The wind-up always shows.
codex.weakness: The lunge goes where you were, not where you are: step sideways as it winds up, then hit it while it recovers. Fragile, and they stagger when struck. Every Nibbler dispersed in a Defence mission pushes the white back a little.

codex.title: Spitter
codex.text: A bloated scrap of the Blank that hangs back and spits globs of white at you. It looks like a Nibbler that ate something it disagreed with, possibly a Nibbler.
codex.habits: Keeps its distance and circles. Every couple of seconds it stops and swells (it grows, shakes and shows a faint aim line), then spits a slow glob at where you stood.
codex.weakness: Sidestep the glob, then close in. Up close it panics and backs off instead of spitting, so stay on it. Thin-skinned: a few solid hits put it down.

codex.title: Letter-moth
codex.text: Moths folded out of unsent letters in the Gutterwoods. Each one carries a few words somebody never had the courage to post. Up close you can sometimes read them. You will wish you had not.
codex.habits: Come in packs and flutter in a loose ring around their target. One at a time they stop, flash red for a moment, and dive in a straight line.
codex.weakness: Paper-thin and knocked far by any hit. Swing as one arrives out of its dive and it is gone. Wide swings and area Ink catch several at once; standing still and waiting for the flash is safer than chasing them.

codex.title: Tithe Enforcer
codex.text: A Concord heavy in iron and gilt who carries a bound Ledger as a shield and believes, sincerely, that everything in it is true. Enforcers collect what the clerks cannot.
codex.habits: Walks in slowly and shrugs off single hits; only every third hit staggers him. In reach, he raises the Ledger while a red ring fills on the ground, then stamps it down on everyone inside.
codex.weakness: The Ledger halves any hit from the front. Circle round and hit his back, or have an ally pull him so he turns away (taunts like Hold the Line work). When the red ring appears, leave it: the slam lands exactly where the ring is.

codex.title: Reedling
codex.text: Marsh mud from the white side of Saltreed that got up and learned to spit. The reed-cutters say they are what the Blank leaves of a drowned word.
codex.habits: Spits like a Spitter, from the boardwalks and the shallows, often in pairs.
codex.weakness: The same tell as a Spitter: they swell before they spit. Sidestep, then wade in; they are slow to back away in the mud.

codex.title: Mill scarecrow
codex.text: Something has been stitching the scarecrows at Old Mill Crossing back together and sending them out with sickles. Nobody has seen the miller since the Blank came. Nobody wants to ask the scarecrows.
codex.habits: Chases and lunges like a Nibbler, with a sickle. It twitches before the swing.
codex.weakness: Watch for the twitch and step out of reach; the sickle swings long but slow. Sturdier than a Nibbler, so keep hitting through its recovery.

codex.title: Guild sellsword
codex.text: Not every blade on the Concord road is the Concord's. Some are Guild members on someone else's contract, and they are very good at not taking it personally.
codex.habits: Fast, and they come in pairs. They close quickly and lunge.
codex.weakness: Keep both in front of you so one cannot lunge from behind while you deal with the other. Their lunge has the same wind-up as a Nibbler's: dodge it and punish the recovery. A taunting ally splits the pair.

codex.title: The Auditor
codex.text: The Concord does not send the Auditor to collect. It sends him to strike things out of the Ledger: streets, families, whole towns. A tall clerk in black and parchment with a quill the size of a lance, who never raises his voice, because he has never needed to. Ninefingers has seen his seal twice. Both times, the town it was stamped on stopped being a town by morning.
codex.habits: Lance thrust: a red lane follows his target, locks and brightens, then he lunges its full length. Ink line: a dotted line with a red wash marks a whole row or column, then the quill sweeps it and the floor there is erased for a few seconds. At half strength he issues a Final Notice: faster wind-ups, thrusts in chains of three, crossed lines and clerks called in.
codex.weakness: Step sideways out of the red lane. After a thrust his nib sticks in the ground: that is the opening, and hits land half again as hard. Never stand on a dotted line when the pen comes. In the second phase, clear the clerks quickly or they will herd you into the lines.

codex.title: The Blank
codex.text: A white, silent nothing that eats whatever it touches: ink, stone, songs, debts, the memory that a place was ever there. It came out of the east and it does not stop. You cannot fight it, any more than you can fight a page being turned. You can only hold the line, and push back where it is thin.

more.text: It never gives anything back. It gave you back. Nobody knows why, least of all you.
Verity Hale stepped into it like a door, and it closed behind her like one.

codex.title: Fray
codex.text: How far the Blank has eaten into a province, from 0 to 100. Fray rises every day at the edge of the white, faster beside land that is already gone, faster where nobody governs, and faster still once a place is past half gone: it feeds itself. Frayed land pays less. At 100 the province is erased.

more.text: What pushes it down: a governor who suits the land, Wardlamps, scouting and patrol missions, and holding the line when a surge comes. Every source is listed in a province's panel on the Command Table.

codex.title: Surges
codex.text: Every few days the Blank gathers itself and lunges at one province. You get a warning, and a Defence mission on the map. Hold the wardstone until the surge breaks and it never lands. Ignore it and the province takes a heavy blow of Fray and a scar that keeps fraying it for days.

more.text: More warning comes from upgrading the Command Table, the Long Watch research, Guild river gossip bought through Diplomacy, and friends who tell you what they hear. A friendly faction can send aid, so a surge lands at half strength.

codex.title: Erased land
codex.text: Land the Blank has finished with. It keeps the outline and eats the rest: Whitewater still has the shape of a village on the map and nothing inside it. Erased provinces produce nothing, cannot be governed, and fray everything next to them faster.

more.text: It can be undone. A Reclaim mission pushes into the white to break the Blot that holds the land, and 3 Ink rewrites it. It comes back thin, unclaimed and at 60 Fray, but it comes back.

codex.title: Verity's plans
codex.text: Every week or so the Blank leans hard on one province for a few days, more than its spread explains. Chalk lines appear on Concord roads. Somebody is aiming it. The pressure shows in the province's panel with how long it lasts and what counters it: a governor halves some of it, a lit Wardlamp stops some of it outright.

more.text: Verity Hale has stopped pretending it is not her. She calls it helping.

codex.title: Wardlamps
codex.text: Lamps lit with Ink on posts at a province's edge. The Blank dislikes being looked at, and a lit Wardlamp lowers the daily Fray of the province it stands in. Build and raise them from the Buildings screen in any province you hold; every level costs more and burns brighter.

codex.title: Ink
codex.text: Ink is what the world is written in, and the only thing the Blank cannot simply eat: it has to unwrite it first. It wells up from the ground at the Wickham spring, comes back from expeditions, and pays for the things that push the white away: Wardlamps, Reclaims, the rarest research. In a hero's hands it becomes magic, in five colours that people can hold and one that only the Blank uses.

codex.title: Red Ink
codex.text: Force. Blows, lunges and blasts that hurt. Red is the colour of every underlined threat and every final demand, and it hits like one.

codex.title: Blue Ink
codex.text: Order. Guards, parries, stuns and holding the line. The colour of the ruled lines on a ledger page, which tell everything written there where it is allowed to go.

codex.title: Gold Ink
codex.text: Debt. Levies, audits and making enemies pay, in every sense. The Concord writes its Ledger in gold, which tells you most of what you need to know about the Concord.

codex.title: Green Ink
codex.text: Mending. Heals, shields and broth. Herbalists' labels and hedge-witch recipes are written in green, and so, Mother Gristle insists, is anything worth surviving.

codex.title: Black Ink
codex.text: Erasure. Shadows, knives and lines struck through. The nearest thing to what the Blank does that a person can hold, which is why the Concord licenses it and everyone who uses it well is unlicensed.

codex.title: White Ink
codex.text: Not ink at all: the absence of it. Only the Blank and the things it makes use White. It does not write anything. It takes the writing away. Nobody in Hollowmark can hold it. Nobody should want to.

more.text: Ilse can. She came out of a looking-glass the Blank forgot to empty, and the white does not seem to know she is there. Her Unwrite takes the weak and the fallen out of the world entirely. She says it feels like reading a page from the back.

codex.title: The Abbey of Saint Ledger
codex.text: Three hundred years of monks copying the Great Ledger by hand, so the world could be written back if the capital's copy burned. They are proud, poor, frightened and owe the Concord everything. The Prioress runs the house. The Abbot runs the books.

more.text: The Abbey stands on the Bonefield Rising's dead: eleven thousand four hundred and six people the Concord struck out of the Ledger. Every abbot knew.
Under Prioress Ebba the Abbey has stopped copying the Ledger. A Friendly Abbey lends its scholars to your research.

codex.title: The Erasers
codex.text: Verity Hale's followers: archivists, clerks and struck-out families who have read the Concord's unedited drafts and want every ledger burned. White coats, tapers, and a list of names read aloud before every fire. They hold the Bonefield Cloister and burn what they can reach.

more.text: First Reader Askew signs the lists. The handwriting is very nice.
While they are hostile, the Erasers make trouble at dawn: a fire in your study, ink spilled from the stores, a forged writ. Win them round or keep them busy.

codex.title: Blotted Penitent
codex.text: A monk of Saint Ledger's who did penance for the blank pages until the Blank accepted it. Still in the habit. Still on its knees, mostly.
codex.habits: Shuffles in, often in pairs, and swings its scourge. Every so often it hunches with both hands out and grabs: whoever it catches is held fast and slowly wiped, and comes out of it Erased.
codex.weakness: The hunch is the warning: step back out of the marked circle. If it gets hold of someone, any hit from a friend makes it let go and reel, wide open. Caught alone, hammer Attack to struggle free sooner.

codex.title: Copyist
codex.text: A scribe the Blank has half eaten, still copying. It carries a quill and an inkpot of nothing and writes the floor out of the world.
codex.habits: Keeps its distance and circles. Every few seconds it kneels and raises its quill: a faint aim line, then a dotted strip with a red wash across where you stand, a row or a column. The strip turns to blank paper for a few seconds and burns anyone standing on it.
codex.weakness: Step off the dotted strip, then run it down. Up close it only shuffles away, and a hit while it kneels spoils the line.

codex.title: Eraser Reader
codex.text: An Eraser who reads the names before the fire, and carries the taper that lights it. Readers fight in pairs and keep reading while they swing.
codex.habits: Comes in pairs and lunges with a lit taper that can set you burning. From a few strides off it stops and reads a name from its ledger: every Eraser in earshot fights harder while it reads, and if it gets to the end of the name it comes for you fast and hits hard.
codex.weakness: Any hit cuts the reading off and staggers it, so go for the Reader first and leave the others until it is quiet. Dodge the lunge after a finished name, then punish the recovery. A quick heal stops the burn ticking.

codex.title: Eraser Whitewasher
codex.text: Erasers with buckets of lime and the Blank stirred in. They whitewash names off walls, and off people.
codex.habits: Hangs back behind the Readers and flings slow globs of whitewash. When you come for it, it dips its brush and slaps a wet white stripe across your way: wade through it and you slow to a crawl and are Erased.
codex.weakness: Hit it while it dips the brush and nothing gets painted. Otherwise walk round the end of the stripe (it is short) and run it down: up close it panics and backs off, and a few hits put it down.

codex.title: The Abbot Who Copied Himself
codex.text: Abbot Wulfstan of Saint Ledger's wrote the first new hymn the Abbey had sung in a hundred years. When the ink stopped holding, he decided to hold it himself, and made several copies of himself to be sure.
codex.habits: Paper copies walk a half-beat behind him and strike short strips of floor out of the world. Up close he draws back his crozier (a red wedge) and sweeps it round. He writes whole rows or columns out of the garth, like the Auditor's line. Every so often the garth flashes white and he re-copies: everyone trades places and torn copies come back. At half strength: more copies, faster re-copies, a ring of gold light that bursts outwards, and penitents.
codex.weakness: Only the real Abbot's hands drip ink, and only he bleeds: hit him, not the paper. A copy tears with one blow, which buys room but nothing else. Leave the red wedge sideways, never stand on a dotted line, and get outside the gold ring before it bursts.

codex.title: The Velvet Nobility
codex.text: The old houses of the Velvet Causeway: dukes, marquises and cousins of both, who own the bridges, the wine and each other's debts. When the Blank came they decided the masquerade should simply not stop. The Duc de Lantenay speaks for them, very slowly.

more.text: The masquerade's host ate a few guests a night, and while it ate, the ink stayed off the bridges. The Nobility knew within a week. The Concord sent the debtors.
The party is over. A Friendly Nobility takes Hollowmark up as its latest fashion and pays patronage in Gilt.

codex.title: Masked Reveller
codex.text: A masquerade guest who has worn the mask so long there is nothing much left under it. Revellers still dance. They have stopped caring who with.
codex.habits: Circles at a distance, then rises on its toes and spins into a waltz dash across the floor, slashing everything on the way. Comes in pairs and threes.
codex.weakness: The rise onto its toes is the tell: step sideways out of the line, and hit it while it is dizzy at the end of the spin. It cannot turn mid-dash.

codex.title: Bridge Duellist
codex.text: The Causeway settles its quarrels on the bridges, at dawn, in public. Some duellists have been settling them for so long that they challenge anything that walks across.
codex.habits: Keeps its guard up: hits from the front glance off its blade. Every so often it raises the sword to its face in a salute, then lunges twice, fast.
codex.weakness: Get round its side or behind it, where the guard does not reach. The salute is the warning: dodge the double lunge, then hit it while it recovers. A stun or a charm opens the guard.

codex.title: Ink Eel
codex.text: Eels made of the ink lake itself, with half-finished words drifting under their skin. Word-fishers hate them: they eat the catch.
codex.habits: Swims under the ground where you cannot hit it. A dark ring opens where it is about to surface, and it comes up through the ring biting.
codex.weakness: Never stand in a ring. It lingers on the surface after a bite: that is when to hit it. Several at once means moving all the time.

codex.title: Lamplighter
codex.text: The Causeway's lamplighters work for whoever pays for the oil. Since the Concord barges started paying, they light other things.
codex.habits: Keeps its distance and lobs oil lanterns. A circle marks where each one will land; it bursts in a ring of fire that can set you burning.
codex.weakness: Step out of the circle before the lantern lands, then close in: up close it swings its pole slowly and has nowhere to run.

codex.title: The Host
codex.text: It came to the masquerade the first night after the Blank arrived, sat down at the head of the table and never left. Nobody invited it. It is mostly mouth, and it wears a mask on every part of itself that could be called a face.
codex.habits: Bites in a wedge in front of it. Spits volleys of words that fly out in a fan. Breathes in, and everything near it slides towards the mouth. Calls revellers to the table and swallows them to heal. At half strength it tears its masks off, breathes in harder, and jumps: a shadow marks where it will land.
codex.weakness: Fight from the sides, outside the bite. Walk away from the inhale, never towards it. Kill the guests it calls before they reach the mouth, or it heals. Leave the shadow before the jump lands, then hit it while it is stuck in the floor.

codex.title: The Harbour Moot
codex.text: The fishing families of the Unfinished Coast, who settle everything that matters in the net loft at Trevail by a show of hands. Loveday Pascoe, harbourmaster, speaks for them when they let her.

more.text: Eleven boats came home to the bell. The Moot has written Hollowmark's name in the harbour book, in the column for people who turned up.
The tide moves again. A Friendly Moot puts Hollowmark on the catch list and sends salt fish every day.

codex.title: Stopped Wave
codex.text: A piece of the stopped sea that has walked off on its own: a wave on legs, curled over at the top, still waiting to break.
codex.habits: Slides in slowly. When it rears up tall, a long strip lights up in front of it, and it crashes down the whole length of the strip. After the crash it lies there as a puddle for a moment, then pulls itself back up.
codex.weakness: Step out of the strip, sideways, never backwards along it. The puddle takes extra damage: hit it while it is flat.

codex.title: Drowned Netter
codex.text: A fisherman who went in after his nets and came out still holding them. He still casts. He is not choosy about the catch.
codex.habits: Keeps a little way off. Whirls its net over its head while a ring follows whoever it is watching, then throws: anyone in the ring is caught and slowed, and it hauls them in for a blow.
codex.weakness: Step out of the ring before it locks. Hit it while it whirls and the throw is spoiled. Ranged hits are best.

codex.title: Half-Gannet
codex.text: A seabird the Blank got half of. The half that is left still dives for fish. It no longer checks whether they are fish.
codex.habits: Circles high where nothing can reach it. Every few seconds it hangs over the spot where someone stands, a ring under its shadow, then folds and drops beak first. It sticks in the sand for a moment after.
codex.weakness: Watch its shadow, not the bird. Leave the ring, then hit it while it is stuck. A hit keeps its beak in the sand a little longer.

codex.title: Salt Wight
codex.text: Someone who drowned off Halfwave before the sea stopped, dried where they stood on the sea bed, and walked ashore crusted white.
codex.habits: Slow and stubborn, with a heavy swing that can sting like brine. The first time it falls it does not die: it crumbles into a heap of salt with a ring round it that fills as it gathers itself.
codex.weakness: Break the heap with any hit before the ring closes, and it is gone. Leave it, and it stands up again at half strength. White Ink unwrites it outright, heap or no heap.

codex.title: Low Water
codex.text: Everything the tide forgot to bring back, gathered at the bottom of Halfwave Bay into one shape taller than a house. Wrecks turn in it. A figurehead uses it for a face.
codex.habits: Sends rolling swells down long marked lanes. Spits a fan of brine. Opens a whirlpool that drags everything towards its middle. Calls stopped waves in. At half strength it sinks into the sand, and the whole bay floods except for a few pale dry banks; then it surfaces where its shadow marks and lies beached for a moment.
codex.weakness: Step out of the lanes sideways. Walk out of the whirlpool, never across it. When the bay is hatched, get onto a dry bank. Hit it hardest while it is beached.

hollowmark.text: A wall, a well, a tavern and a few hundred people pretending the horizon is not getting closer. The Concord ran it from the tax office until the Blank ate the tax office.

Since the takeover it has no governor, no tax office and no legal standing, and it is run from the Command Table in the square by someone who officially does not exist. It has never been happier, or in more danger.

meadow.text: Where you crawled out of the white. The Nibblers still come back to the spot, as if they lost something there.

gutterwoods.text: Every unsent letter in the Inklands takes root here sooner or later. The leaves rustle in handwriting. Listen too long and you start to recognise the hands.

oldmill.text: It grinds nothing now. The granary was looted long before anyone thought to blame the Blank, and the scarecrows have started walking the furrows at night.
Where Tithe-Captain Morrow's column came to collect Hollowmark, and left without it.

lampwick.text: The spring is black and slow and never runs dry. Everything that is hungry for writing finds its way to it sooner or later, the Blank included.

saltreed.text: Stilt-houses and boardwalks over a marsh going white from the east. The reed-cutters work the half that is still green and do not go near the white half, which has started saying their names.

gallows.text: The gallows the ferry is named for have not been used in years. The Guild finds that the name does most of the work.

tithe.text: The Concord's last tollhouse before the Marches. Most travellers are found wanting. The rest are found later, in ditches, with their paperwork in order.
The tollgate where the Auditor fell. The clerks have filed the incident under weather.

whitewater.text: It had a millrace, a chapel and a name. On the map it is still drawn in. On the ground there is nothing to stand on.

candlemere.text: A lake town of chandlers. Every window burns all night, just in case.
Five wax barges lie burnt at the bottom of the lake. The sixth made it to the Abbey. Nell Tapper keeps the wicks going for whoever holds the town.

abbey.text: The Abbey of Saint Ledger, its cloister walk, its copying hall and its bells.
The bells ring one hour at a time again. The brothers copy Osyth's board now, with the heading put back.

ossuary.text: A cloister on a hill the Ledger says was always empty. The Erasers camp in its garth.
Under the hill: eleven thousand four hundred and six, counted, in chalk.

quillpine.text: A pilgrims' hostel and a lot of pines. The road east ends in white.

lanternquay.text: Lantern Quay, the Causeway's working wharf, where the barges unload and the lamps are hung so that nobody's face is lit.
The Concord barge lies on the bottom off the smugglers' wharf with its steel table still on deck. The boatmen row round it.

causeway.text: The Velvet Causeway itself: bridges, balconies, the masquerade hall and the duelling bridges.
The candles are out. People stand on the bridges with their masks off, looking at each other's faces.

inkmere.text: Pendower Shallows, where word-fishers net words out of the ink lake and sell them by the pound.
Out on the flats there used to be a little brick house that was never built. It went with the last verse of a song.

terraces.text: The Vauclair Terraces, vineyards that send their wine to the masquerade. The grapes have started to taste of paper.
The Office of Corrections' school on the Terraces stands empty, its dormitory door broken from the inside out.

saltgrave.text: Trevail Harbour, built up a cliff, with a shipyard, a net loft and a bell tower on the quay. The Moot meets in the net loft.
A wave hangs over the whole town, green at the bottom and white at the top. Washing dries on hooks on its underside. The bell is rung every hour, all night, for the boats still out.

halfwave.text: Halfwave Bay, where the sea stopped twenty yards short of the beach and stands there in a long green wall.
The chapel's looking-glass is empty now. The fishing families have started looking into it again on Sundays, to see if anyone else is in there.
The tide moves a hand's width a day. Children sit on the sand and watch it come, which is the most exciting thing that has happened at Halfwave in years.

lighthouse.text: Polgarrow Light, on a black rock at the end of the land. Below it the spray of a breaking wave stands in a white fan, every drop in place.
The lamp is lit. Jory Hocking keeps his log again, every hour, and does not remember the five days he spent talking.

figures.name: Verity Hale
figures.title: the archivist in the white
figures.text: A woman in a pale archivist's coat who watches the Blank eat the way other people watch a sunset. She called you 'the one it gave back', apologised for the tax office (not very sincerely), and walked into the white as if it were a door.

more.text: Chalk lines on Concord roads, and the Blank leaning harder wherever they point. She is aiming it.

Her letter says she is not your enemy: she is the person who has read the drafts, and when you have read them too, you will agree about the Concord. It asks you to stop pushing the white back. It is signed 'Fondly'. Polite letters are the worst kind.

figures.name: The Auditor
figures.title: of the Office of Corrections
figures.text: The Concord's answer to towns that will not file. He strikes things out of the Ledger with a quill the size of a lance. See the Codex for how he fights.

more.text: Struck out at the Tithe Road tollgate. Verity Hale sent her thanks: he had erased four towns she was fond of.

figures.name: Governor Thale
figures.title: formerly of Hollowmark
figures.text: The Concord's governor of Hollowmark, until the morning after the tax office went white. He took the town seal, his carriage and every report he would ever need to write, and left the town behind. He is presumably still writing them.

figures.name: Clerk Pettigrew
figures.title: of the Hollowmark tax office
figures.text: The clerk who tried to write you into the Ledger and found nothing there to write. He checked twice, then once more in better light. Whether the Blank took him with the office, nobody has thought to check, which in Hollowmark counts as an obituary.

figures.name: Tithe-Captain Morrow
figures.title: of the Concord tithe columns
figures.text: He counts people the way other men count sheep, Ninefingers says, and he came to Old Mill Crossing to count Hollowmark.

more.text: His column broke at the Crossing. In his papers was the order with the Auditor's red seal.
Ash handed him back his empty strongbox and let him walk home. He said he owed you one, and that he does not write that down for anybody.
He walked home in his stockings. His boots went to market and his ledger to Quill, who calls it the dullest book he has ever loved.
Ash stood aside for Mother Gristle's tonic. He walked home on his own feet, issuing a receipt for every hiccup.
Third Under-Clerk at the Tithe Office in the Crossing now, and writing to you. He sharpens the pens, and reads everything they are sharpened for.

figures.name: Abbot Wulfstan
figures.title: of Saint Ledger's
figures.text: Abbot of Saint Ledger's for thirty years. He has his monks copy the Ledger day and night and writes the hours on the air himself.

more.text: Found among his copies by the ink on his hands. Buried by the Founders' Door, with the eleven thousand.

figures.name: Prioress Ebba
figures.title: of Saint Ledger's
figures.text: Keeps the Abbey's house while the Abbot keeps its books. Dry, exact, and very tired of being polite to the Concord.

more.text: Runs the Abbey now. Has stopped it copying the Ledger.

figures.name: Brother Odo
figures.title: messenger of Saint Ledger's
figures.text: Walked to the Concord for help and was sent back with a receipt. Walked to you instead.

figures.name: Askew
figures.title: First Reader of the Erasers
figures.text: Signs the Erasers' lists of names in a careful hand. Reads one aloud before every fire, so that somebody has said it.

more.text: Left the Bonefield camp before you broke it. Did not leave the fire.

figures.name: The Duc de Lantenay
figures.title: of the Velvet Nobility
figures.text: Seventy, white-wigged, perfectly polite and perfectly cold. Holds the stairs at the masquerade and calls the courses.

more.text: Speaks for the Nobility now the party is over, mostly in paperwork.

figures.name: Purser Gaudin
figures.title: of the Office of Corrections
figures.text: The Concord officer who ran the barge to the masquerade's back stairs, and who signed the letter Hortense read aloud. A man doing his job.

figures.name: Bérénice de Saulx
figures.title: Hortense's sister
figures.text: Held six years by the Office of Corrections as surety for the de Saulx debts, copying contracts. Writes in code. Thinks the fan code was stupid.

figures.name: Old Pratt
figures.title: moneylender of Lantern Quay
figures.text: Holds five hundred and twelve contracts in a strongbox on the smugglers' wharf, or did. Charges forty per cent a month and calls everyone 'my dear'.

figures.name: Loveday Pascoe
figures.title: harbourmaster of Trevail
figures.text: Runs Trevail Harbour and its harbour book, rings its bell and speaks for the Moot when they let her. Sawed a piece off the sea to make a point.

more.text: Eleven home, twenty-one out. She rings the bell every hour for the twenty-one.

figures.name: Jory Hocking
figures.title: keeper of Polgarrow Light
figures.text: Forty years keeping Polgarrow Light. Kerra's father. Went up to the lamp the night the sea stopped, and did not come down.

more.text: Spoke for five days in a voice that was not his, about plates and suppers and a door. Remembers none of it. Keeps his log again.
